issues.description: The problem statement and template require a public method named singFarmSong() in Farm that plays the song for all animals, but the solution implements a public method named playFarmSong() instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the template and spec will implement/expect singFarmSong(), while the solution exposes a different public API, causing confusion and potential test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the public API across artifacts. Rename the solution's playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() wrapper in the solution that delegates to playFarmSong(). Ensure the template, problem statement, and solution all use the same method name (singFarmSong) and signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and template define/expect a public Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the solution implementation uses a differently named public method playFarmSong(). This renaming of the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) across artifacts creates a mapping barrier for students: they will look for/implement singFarmSong() based on the assignment and template, yet the reference solution exposes playFarmSong(), causing confusion and possible test mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() (and update any internal calls accordingly), or alternatively change the template/problem statement to reference playFarmSong()—preferably align the solution to the problem/template by implementing public void singFarmSong().
